documents.name: CyberKit4SME
documents.textPreview: 1 This project is funded by the European Union H2020-SU-DS-2019 Digital Security and privacy for citizens and Small and Medium Enterprises and Micro Enterprises CyberKit4SME Democratizing a Cyber Security Toolkit for SMEs and MEs Project Nº 883188 Project Summary CyberKit4SME aims to democratize a kit of cybersecurity tools and methods enabling SMEs/MEs to: Increase awareness of cybersecurity risks, vulnerabilities and attacks; Monitor and forecast risks; Manage risks using organisational, human and technical security measures with greater confidence; and Collaborate and share information in a collective security and data protection effort. Tools developed in the project are: Semi-automated ISO 27005 threat identification and risk mitigation analysis, using a knowledge base of technical and human/organisational risk factors; Encryption and isolation tools to protect data being stored, processed or exchanged; Security information and event management, using multiple data sources for threat detection and diagnosis, Blockchain tools for SMEs/MEs to share intelligence and incident reports with supply chain partners and with CERTs. CyberKit4SME will make its tools cheaper and more usable by SME/ME, by 1) Exploiting synergies between tools in the kit to simplify the use of each; 2) Sharing information to increase the data available for threat detection and diagnosis at each SME/ME; 3) Embedding intelligence (e.g. machine reasoning and data analytics), to fill gaps in inputs and automate tasks such as risk analysis and security configuration. The project will also use its tools and cyber range demos to train SMEs/MEs to identify their top threats and recognise and address them with greater confidence. Results will be 2 validated by SME/ME in four critical sectors: Finance, Health Care, Energy and Transport. Outcomes include reducing the time/cost of cybersecurity awareness and protection, simplifying meeting and demonstrating compliance with NIS Directive and GDPR, protecting distributed assets from cloud services to edge devices, and engaging insecure supply chains with larger organisations. The project will also collaborate with related research projects and disseminate widely in the scientific community and in SME networks. In figure 1 is presented the overall concept of the CyberKit4SME project. It will produce offline risk modelling tools to support ISO 27005 risk analysis and privacy and data- protection ‘by design’, covering technical, organisational and human risk factors, and supporting regulatory compliance analysis and compliance documentation generation. Also, the project will provide online cyber security risk monitoring based on collaborative security intelligence and event management (SIEM) tool, and data protection measures designed for easy access that will be effective in cloud environments. Cybersecurity incident reporting and security intelligence sharing will be supported by a secure, privacy-aware blockchain framework, allowing SMEs to collaborate with CERTs, supply chain partners and indirectly, other SMEs to detect and address threats in critical sectors without fear of reputational damage. These tools will be supported by training including cyber range demonstrations, raising awareness and encouraging adoption of advanced cybersecurity methods by SMEs and MEs. CyberKit4SME will thus increase awareness of cybersecurity threats, vulnerabilities Figure 1. CyberKit4SME Overall Concept 3 and risks among SMEs and MEs, allow more confident and effective forecasting, monitoring and management of those risks, and simplify compliance with regulatory obligations under the GDPR and NIS Directive, as well as sector-specific regulations relating to security, data protection and privacy. CyberKit4SME will validate its tools with SMEs in four critical sectors: finance, healthcare, energy and transportation. Project vision The overall aim of CyberKit4SME is to democratize advanced cyber security methods for SMEs and MEs, in order to: • Enable SMEs and MEs to monitor and forecast cybersecurity risks by equipping them with advanced, but low-cost and easy-to-use tools that will allow them to both assess the cybersecurity risks of their business’s IT infrastructure at design-time (following an asset-based risk assessment approach aligned with ISO 27005) and to monitor and update risk level assessments in real-time to detect potential threats without frequent recourse to expensive cybersecurity experts including consultants. • Raise SMEs and MEs’ awareness of cybersecurity risks, vulnerabilities and attacks through training in the use of these tools, and by analysing organisational and human factors that affect risk levels in their business; making educational material available for their employees to promote safe behaviour; facilitating their participation to cyber ranges as part of the training experience, and fostering a resilient community of SMEs and MEs by promoting information exchange with CERT/CSIRTs and other SMEs and MEs on cybersecurity incidents. • Support SMEs and MEs to manage their security, privacy and personal data protection risks by providing a wide-ranging set of tools that will allow them to implement risk mitigation measures based on a sophisticated risk analyses for their information networks, including end-to-end data protection using advanced encryption techniques to ensure confidentiality and integrity for data stored, transferred and processed onsite or in the cloud, and SIEM technology to help them prevent, detect and recover from cyber-attacks. • Equip SMEs and MEs with an online collaborative, security information sharing and incident reporting system by providing a blockchain platform through which SMEs and MEs will be able to securely share cybersecurity information in supply chains and with CERTS to improve risk monitoring and facilitate preparedness and responses to cyber-attacks, engage in a collective response to cyber security risks, and implement mandatory cybersecurity incident reporting. The CyberKit4SME project aims to demonstrate these tools working in an operational environment based on SME partners’ existing product and service testing environments, and with users fulfilling their normal business roles. It will also take the necessary actions to ensure the tools provided will be commercially sustainable and can be made available to a wide range of SMEs and MEs following the project. 4 Expected project’s impact The work programme for H2020-SU-DS03 identifies four main impacts. CyberKit4SME will contribute to all of them, as outlined below: • SMEs/MEs are better protected and become active players in the Digital Single Market including implementation of the NIS Directive and GDPR • Security, privacy and personal data protection are strengthened as a shared responsibility • Reduced economic damage caused by harmful cyber-attacks and data (including personal data) protection breaches • Pave the way for a trustworthy EU digital environment benefitting all economic and social actors List of participants Participant No Participant organisation name Country 1 (Coordinator) Grupo Corporativo GFI Informática SA ES 2 University of Southampton UK 3 IBM Israel – Science and Technology LTD IL 4 SINTEF NO 5 SOGEI IT 6 Tiani Spirit AT 7 Energis BE 8 JRC Capital Management Consultancy & Research DE 9 Elektrobit RO 10 3Soft RO Project general information: Project duration: The project duration is 3 years. It started on 1 June 2020 and will last till 31 May 2023. Project website: https://cyberkit4sme.eu/ EU official project page: https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/883188

documents.name: DANUBIUS Preparatory Phase for the pan-European Research Infrastructure
documents.textPreview: Grant Agreement number: 739562 Project acronym: DANUBIUS-PP Project title: Preparatory Phase for the pan-European Research Infrastructure DANUBIUS–RI “The International Centre for advanced studies on river-sea systems” Call: H2020-INFRADEV-2016-2 Start date of the project: 1 December 2016 Duration of the project: 36 months Coordinator: Institutul National de Cercetare Dezvoltare pentru Geologie si GeoEcologie Marina – GeoEcoMar, ROMANIA Consortium: 30 partners from 16 countries, including 2 ERICs (ICOS & EMSO) Total Budget: 3.997.592 euro Project website address: http://www.danubius-pp.eu/ Main Results: - DANUBIUS-RI_Science_Agenda - DANUBIUS-RI Videos Dissemination materials: - Flyer - Brochure DANUBIUS-PP was a three -year project dedicated to raise DANUBIUS -RI (International Centre for Advanced Studies on River -Sea Systems) to the legal, financial and technical maturity required for successful implementation and development. It represents the financial sup port granted by the European Commission to the DANUBIUS -RI consortium, aimed at consolidating DANUBIUS -RI. DANUBIUS-RI is a pan-European distributed research infrastructure (RI) building on existing expertise to support interdisciplinary research on river-sea (RS) systems, spanning the environmental, social and economic sciences, included in the ESFRI Roadmap in 2016. As a distributed RI that brings together world leading expertise, it will provide access to a range of RS systems, facilities and expertise across Europe, to provide a ‘one-stop shop’ for knowledge exchange, access to harmonised data, a platform for interdisciplinary research, education and training and hence provide answers to questions regarding sustainable management and environmental protection of the RS continuum. The Consortium achieved the objectives set in the proposal, as it consolidated during these 36 months of cooperation and collaboration for reaching one common goal: DANUBIUS-RI. The DANUBIUS -PP specific objectives (as presented in the DoA) were fulfilled as described in the following lines: (i) Establish the political and financial commitments from countries willing to be part of DANUBIUS-RI and national stakeholders to deliver the key operational components of the RI. The budgetary requirements for the development and implementation of the RI will be defined within the context of the social and economic impacts and benefits for nations individually (what is in for them) and Europe as a whole. This will be used as the evidence- base to secure sustainable income streams for the developing RI. This specific objective was achieved in the second half of the project with the Board of Governmental Representatives (BGR) playing a major role in identifying and resolving poten tial differences and agreeing a set of ERIC statutes to be submitted (step 1) in early 2020 . BGR debated, negotiated and agreed on a series of DANUBIUS -PP deliverables, mainly in regards to the Science and Innovation Agenda, list of services to be provided by the RI, detailed business model and foreseen construction and operational costs for the RI, detailed architecture aspects (with distribution of components in various countries). The final Stakeholder Event , held in Rome in November 2020, brought vital information concerning specific needs of the various categories of stakeholders, mainly those from outside the academic world (business and decision makers). Since the unanimous approval of the text of DANUBIUS -ERIC statutes at the 6 th BGR meeting, Letters of Intent from countries interested in signing the ERIC have been collected from several states (Italy, Czech Republic, Ukraine), others being in course of approval (Germany, Netherlands, Spain, Bulgaria, Hungary, Ireland). UK government r epresentatives, actively involved in the ERIC process, announced that they will continue to strongly support the development of DANUBIUS-ERIC, but, due to the Brexit process, there is a high level of uncertainty on the possibility to sign a LoI for Step 1. During the PP – interest was raised in DANUBIUS -RI also in Lithuania, who is on track to include the facility on the national roadmap. (ii) Grow the reputation and linkages of the RI within Europe and Internationally. Outreach and growth of the RI are core to the sustainability of the RI. Here growth is considered at two levels: a) wider engagement within the European scientific communities, including other ESFRIs; and b) international outreach and growth, maximising the impact of DANUBIUS-RI as a world leadi ng RI, drawing upon recent interest expressed by countries of the Mekong River Basin. The Consortium has continued to be actively involved in making the European research community aware of the project. Involvement in ENVRI+ has included participation in t raining activities, membership of BEERi. The DANUBIUS-RI consortium was included and is now part of the ENVRI-FAIR project. The Stakeholder Event in Rome November 2019 was jointly organized with EMSO -ERIC, EMBRC-ERIC, ICOS-ERIC, LifeWatch-ERIC and eLTER, as an exercise of common work and cooperation in the stakeholder engagement process. During the Official Launch of the Black Sea Strategic Research and Innovation Agenda (event of the Romanian Presidency of the EU Council), the relevant ERICs were brought to the attention of the wider Black Sea community by the coordinator of DANUBIUS -PP ( also organizer of the conference). A dedicated section was dedicated to the marine ERICs and EMSO-ERIC, EMBRC-ERIC, EURO ARGO ERIC, LifeWatch ERIC and ICOS ERIC where the relevant opportunities of European RIs and international dimensions were stressed. Th e coordinating country (Romania) also stressed the importance of DANUBIUS-RI in a series of talks with the United States NSF during the ongoing discussions for a joint environmental research and education programme. DANUBIUS-RI – through the PP consortium - has been actively involved in discussions and activities with Water JPI. DANUBIUS-PP representatives have been engaged in the various Water JPI events and discussions are being held to prepare dedicated calls that could be developed with the support of existing European RIs. DANUBIUS-RI was presented and its representatives were actively involved in a series of high level international conferences on the relevant topics of DANUBIUS-RI. These activities have increased out profile and increased our links with other environmental RIs and the European e -infrastructure community.. (iii) Further detail and develop the DANUBIUS -RI science and innovation agenda and, where appropriate, leading the state-of-the-art science and technological developments. Critical to this objective is being demonstrably responsive to the continually evolving societal, user and stakeholder requirements. This objective will put in place an innovative and progressive looking science programme to meet existing and emerging societal ch allenges. The evolving science and innovation agenda will feed initiatives to secure national and European funding to support research and innovation initiatives. Development and production of the Science and Innovation Agenda (SIA) was one of the most challenging tasks in this project and was completed during the second reporting period . A Scientific Case Study was submitted alongside the DANUBIUS-RI ESFRI proposal back in 2015, but further details and updating were needed (to provide opportunities for wider engagement in developing the scientific rationale for the RI). The SIA was the main objective of WP 2, in close cooperation with other WPs like WP4 – (to define the services offered by DANUBIUS -RI to the research community), WP5 – Architecture, WP6, and WP8 – ICT infrastructure. The SIA presents challenges and research needs, as identified by DANUBIUS -RI, for achieving healthy River-Sea Systems. It highlights research priorities for the first five years of DANUBIUS -RI’s operation and outlines the scien tific challenges and research needs that will shape the development of the infrastructure to ensure it provides the interdisciplinary expertise, tools and capacities required. (iv) Further development of the architecture of the organisational and administrative components of the RI and its legal identity. The respective roles of the Hub, the Nodes, the Supersites, the Technology Transfer Office and the Data Centre will be defined. Central to the organisational structure are: a) development of elements of the infrastructure; (b) formulation of the digital and non-digital data management strategies; c) development of the administrative agreements; and d) assessment of the resource gaps including human capital and expertise and establish associated training programmes to deliver these gaps. The main architecture for DANUBIUS -RI was developed in the first 18 months . During the second reporting period work was undertaken on further defining organisational and procedural policy for Nodes, Technology Transfer Office, ICT e-infrastructure and e-Learning Office. It was decided to adopt a different architecture than was originally envisaged for Technology Transfer Office. In the light of the complex European legal landscape related to IPR, it was agreed that the Technnology Transfer Office should have coordination, policy and advisory roles, with technology transfer actions undertaken at national level. E-education services were grouped under a new component – the e-Learning Office and activities have started on preparing contents for this new element. A Data Policy was prepared, delivered to - and discussed by the BGR. Specific costs and estimated human resources needs were prepared (WP4 deliverables. Plans for joint training were sketched. In addition, principles and criteria were agreed for the future evolution of the RI to ensure that timely changes could be made without problems. (v) Agree upon the operational requirements of DANUBIUS-RI and its legal identity, including: a) a welldefined access policy that facilitates the advancement of science and innovation both within the public and private sectors, including blue growth, and prom otes societal engagement in environmental stewardship including citizen science; b) common scientific standards and operating procedures to facilitate data comparability within and between existing and new Supersites; and c) translation of the scientific p rogramme, policy and procedures into the DANUBIUS Commons. During the reporting period considerable progress was made on building a set of DANUBIUS Commons and developing a concept for benchmarking and performance. QA procedures were agreed and an interim Quality Assurance Panel set up. An important development was completion of the access policy reference document. Service Level Agreements between DANUBIUS-RI components and the ERIC were delivered, discussed and endorsed by the BGR. A final version will b e approved only in the final stage of ERIC development process. The rationale for DANUBIUS-PP was to raise DANUBIUS-RI to the legal, financial and technical maturity required for successful implementation and development. The ten Work Packages addressed the seven technical elements of DANUBIUS-PPs essential for the construction and operational phases of the RI: (i) project management and planning; (ii) scientific programme and user needs; (iii) legal, governance and organisational; (iv) technical; (v) f inancial and economic; (vi) communication; and (vii) outreach. These elements are addressed in DANUBIUS-PP by ten work packages (WPs). WP 1 managed the consortium and ensured that the work programme objectives , milestones and deliverables were met in a timely manner, while conforming to the DoA. WP2 delivered the Science and Innovation Agenda, working closely with the stakeholder and user communities to ensure that DANUBIUS-RI is structured to meet the societal and environmental challen ges related to RS systems. Preparing a distributed European RI, WP3 defined the optimal operating legal framework for DANUBIUS-RI. It developed the ERIC statutes and operating procedures to manage the RI effectively. WP4 developed the sustainable funding model , listed the specific services, related specific costs for the construction and operation phases and access policies. The architecture including membership, internal functioning and interaction of the component parts of DANUBIUS -RI (the Hub, Nodes, Supersites, Data C entre, Technology Transfer Office , and e -Learning Office ) were defined in WP5. Quality and consistency in the outputs from the RI were assured through the DANUBIUS-Commons in WP6, which also provided the list of relevant KPIs that will monitor the proper functioning of the infrastructure. The protocols for handling, processing and sharing data were developed in WP7 including technical protocols for handling, formatting, processing data within and beyond the RI, including Copernicus and GEOSS. This WP covered protocols both for digital and non-digital data. Requirements for delivering the ICT e-infrastructures and digital data storage were driven by WP8, taking account of the needs of High Performance and Cloud computing, including Adaptive Virt ual Research Environments, following the FAIR principles and the new opportunities offered by the EOSC. Capacity building was the primary objective of WP9 and dissemination and communication the objectives of WP10. From DANUBIUS-PP to DANUBIUS-RI DANUBIUS-RI is now in the final stages of its Preparatory Phase. DANUBIUS -PP was a three -year project, started in December 2016, funded by the European Union’s Horizon 2020 Research and Innovation Programme under Grant Agreement No 739562 aiming to raise DANUBIUS-RI to the legal, financial and technical maturity required for successful implementation and development. DANUBIUS-PP brought together key stakeholders through a process of wide engagement. The Consortium was led by Romania and was composed of 30 partners from 16 countries, with expressions of interest and support from the scientific community in many other countries in Europe and worldwide. The Consortium provided a well balanced mix of competencies required to build DANUBIUS-RI, in terms of both scientific and administrative domains, as well as geographical coverage. DANUBIUS-PP aimed at developing the structures and processes to ensure that the RI strengthens scientific performance by providing a sustainable basis for future operation, delivering key services to the different user communities. GeoEcoMar was the general coordinator of DANUBIUS-PP, being involved in all the WPs of the project and having a total budget of 373.00 euro, and is also the coordinator of the ESFRI project DANUBIUS-RI.

Despre proiect ■ Titlul proiectului: Demand Response in Block of Buildings — DR-BOB ■ Program: Horizon 2020 ■ Durata: 36 luni ■ Valoarea proiectului: 5.136.769 euro ■ Coordonator: Teesside University, UK ■ Parteneri: 10 – Franța (Centre Scientifique Et Technique Du Batiment, Nobatek, Gridpocket SAS), Italia (R2M Solution SRL, Fondazione Poliambulanza), Olanda (Duneworks BV), UK (Teesside University, Siemens Public Limited Company), România (Servelect ESCO, Universitatea Tehnică din Cluj-Napoca). 3 Despre proiect Soluția Proiectul DR-BOB a implementat instrumentele și tehnicile necesare pentru controlul curbei de consum în ansamblurile de clădiri. Soluția de control a curbei de consum se bazează pe optimizarea în timp real a producției, consumului și stocării locale a energiei. Provocarea Sistemele energetice sunt ineficiente și costisitoare, deoarece de cele mai multe ori cererea depășește capacitatea. Blocurile de clădiri oferă mai multă flexibilitate în temporizarea utilizării energiei, în producerea locală de energie și în stocarea de energie față de clădirile individuale. Dar, lipsa de produse și tehnologii adecvate face acest lucru problematic. documents.name: Deracemizarea prin Cristalizare a Compusilor Chirali
documents.textPreview: Deracemizarea prin Cristalizare a Compusilor Chirali. Project number: 722456 CORE: TeraCrystal este o Companie de Cercetare pe bază de Contract (CRO-Contract Reseach Organization) româno-finlandeză, care furnizează servicii de cercetare/dezvoltare pentru industria farmaceutică, una din putinele companii Conștientizând importanta pe care domeniul Pharma îl are in actualul context mondial şi bazându-se pe capacități științifice si de business de cel mai înalt nivel, in anul 2013 a fost incorporata o companie specializata in studiul cristalizării si stării solide pentru compușii farmaceutici activi TeraCrystal a avut la baza transferul de know-how generat prin proiectul HT–Pharma „METODOLOGII MODERNE DE TIP HIGH-THROUGHPUT PENTRU OBŢINEREA ŞI CARACTERIZAREA DE NOI FORME SOLIDE ALE COMPUŞILOR FARMACEUTICI”, finanțare obtinuta de Institutul Naţional de Cercetare Dezvoltare pentru Tehnologii Izotopice şi Moleculare din Cluj-Napoca (INCDTIM) din fonduri structurale POSCCE. Echipa de m anagement, compusa din cercetători de origine romana si finlandeza cu experiența internaționala recunoscuta in domeniu a optat pentru un model de business axat pe două direcții: 1. Servicii specializate de R&D, pentru industria farmaceutică, care să susțină operațiile curente și care să finanțeze programele R&D interne. 2. Cercetare și inovare proprie, care să genereze proprietate intelectuală și implicit sa conduca la crsterea valorii de piata a companiei. Odată cu dezvoltarea companiei au aparut oportunități de colaborare consortii internationale de cer cetare in domeniul cristalizării compusilor farmaceutici. Astfel, in anul 2016 TeraCrystal a fost invitata sa paricipe in proiectul CORE (www.coreitn.eu), proiect care a fost finantat prin programul Horizon 2 020, acțiunea MARIE SKŁODOWSKA-CURIE, Innovative Training Networks (ITN). Proiectul CORE s -a derulat p e durata a 4 ani incepind cu 1 Octombrie 2016 si avind ca tematica Deracemizarea prin Cristalizare a Compusilor Chirali. CORE s-a constituit ca un program ex igent si provocator de training in cerce tare-dezvoltare a 15 doctoranzi, program finalizat cu sustinerea de catre acestia a tezelor de doctorat. Cei 15 doctoranzi, recrutati atit din spatial European cit si din tari associate au beneficiat pe parcursul celor 4 ani de acces la infrastructura de top si instruire de exceptie din partea unor personalitati stiintifice de marca in domeniul Stării solide si Cristalizarii. Totodata, componente cheie ale proiectului CORE au fost stagiile de pregatire in Depart amentele de Cercetare-Dezvoltare ale partenerilor industriali, unde au intrat in contact cu cerintele si exigentele programelor de cercetare aplicata Consorțiul a fost condus de Universitatea Strathclyde Glasgow , coordonator prof. Joop Ter Horst , fiind alcătuit din 7 parteneri academici apartinind un iversitatilor de top din Europa, doi experti si 8 parteneri industriali cu cercetari consistente in Inginerie Chimica, Chimie si Fizica aplicata, dupa cum urmeaza: Parteneri Academici Universitatea Strathclyde, Glasgow UK Strathxlyde Institute of Pharmacy and Biomedical Science Otto-von-Guericke University Magdeburg DE Institute of Process Engineering Universitatea Rouen FR SMS Science et Methode Separatives Universitatea Radbound, Nijmegen NL Institute for Molecules and Materials ETH Zürich CH Institute of Process Engineering Universitatea Manchester UK School of Chemical Engineering and Analytical Science Friedrich-Alexander University of Erlangen- Nuernberg DE Institute of Organic Chemistry Parteneri industriali Max Planck Institute DE TeraCrystal RO Process Systems Engineering UK ChemConnection NL Merck KGaA DE Corbion Purac NL Syncom NL Seqens FR Core team In calitatea sa de partener industrial TeraCrystal a avut responsabitatea de organizarea in perioada 6-10 Noiembrie 2017, la Cluj-Napoca, a unuia din cele 3 Workshopuri prevazute in proiect si anume “Studiul Starii Solide”. La eveniment au participat 50 persoane: cei 15 doctoranz i si conducatorii lor de doctorat, carora li s-au adaugat reprezentantii parterilor industriali si expertii. Workshopul a avut ca obiectiv principal traning in urmatoarele domenii vitale pentru studiul Starii solide si a procesului de Cristalizare si anume: - Difractie de Raze X (XRD) - Rezonanta Magnetica Nucleara (RMN) - Diagrama de faze - Proprietate Intelectuala La organizare si -a adus contributia si Institutul Naţional de Cercetare Dezvoltare pentru Tehnologii Izotopice şi Moleculare din Cluj-Napoca (INCDTIM), evenimentul contribuind la cresterea vizibilitatii institutului si la stabilirea de legaturi institutionale cu universitati si parteneri industriali de renume. Echipa Core XRD trainig-Dr. Mihaela Pop, TeraCystal RMN training-dr. Claudiu Filip, INCDTIM Studiul structurii cristaline Totodată, TeraCrystal a organizat pentru membrii echipei Core, diverse actiuni menite sa promoveze obiectivele istorice si turistice din regiunea Clujului. Astfel au fos t vizitate Muzeul Național de Istorie a Transilvaniei, Muzeul de National de Arta , Gradina Botanica, Catedrala Ortodoxa, Piata Unirii. Deasemeni, participanții au putut aprecia savuroasa gastronomie transilvaneana care s -a bucurat de mult succes. Dar cea mai spectaculosa vizita a fost la Salina Turda, pentru care invitatii au avut un interes dosebit deoarece a constitut un obiectiv turistic special. Mai multe poze se pot viziona la adresa https://www.flickr.com/photos/coreitn/sets/72157662337884418/ Catedrala Ortodoxa Gradina botanica Vizita la Salina Turda In 2018 TeraCrystal a găzduit pe timp de o luna 3 doctoranzi si anume: Giuseppe Belletti, Jan -Joris Devogelaer, and Aliou Mbodji. Scopul principal al stagiulu i a fost familiarizarea celor trei cu fluxul de lucru implemetat la TeraCrystal pentru studiul Starii solide si Cristalizarii a compusilor farmaceutici activi. Totdata doctoranzii au luat cunostinta de mentalitatea si exigentele unui program comercial de cercetare. Subiecte precum productivitate, eficiența, restricțiile de timp, viabilitatea unui plan și alte provocări au fost prezentate și discutate temeinic. Într -un proiect comercial, cea mai im portantă lecție este să că interesul științific nu va fi întotdeauna prima prioritate și va rămâne pe plan secund în majoritatea cazurilor. Rețeaua de clienti, lucrul cu colaboratorii, gestionarea proiectelor și rezolvarea problemelor sub presiunea timpului sunt toate abilități esențiale pentru un cercetător , un proiect comercial implicând echipe multidisciplinare și solicitând flexibilitate și deschidere. Guseppe si Aliou in laboratorul de cristalizare si Polimorfism, TeraCrystal De asemenea, studentii folosit unul dintre proiectele interne de cercetare, ca studiu de caz pentru algoritmul de predicție dezvoltat de Jan -Joris, iar acest lucru arată deja un s ucces experimental de succes care se va exploata in comun. Concluzionind, abilitățile învățate în laboratorul TeraCrystal îi vor ajuta pe Aliou, Giuseppe și Jan-Joris să iși aleagă și să iși urmeze carierele individuale în mediul academic sau industrial. Mihaela Pop, Aliou, Gussepe si Jan-Joris savurind excelenta bere locala

documents.textPreview: EBSIS - Event Based Systems in Iaşi UnTwinning întreUniversitateaAlexandruIoan Cuza din Iaşi, Université de Neuchâtel, T echnische Universität Dresden şi Université catholique de Louvain Proiect desfăşurat în perioada 2016-2018 cadrul programului Horizon 2020 Topic “Spreading Excellence and Widening Participation” – acţiuni Twinning EBSIS – Event Based Systems în Iaşi Consorţiu: • Coordonator: Universitatea Alexandru Ioan Cuza din Iaşi (UAIC – România) • Université de Neuchâtel (UNINE - Elveţia) • Technische Universität Dresden (TUD - Germania) • Université catholique de Louvain (UCL - Belgia) EBSIS – Obiective principale • O1: Obţinerea unui influx de cunoştinţe în instituţia coordonator în domeniul ţintă al proiectului cu sprijin din partea partenerilor externi. Crearea de premize pentru acţiuni cooperative de cercetare şi colaborări ulterioare. • O2: Creşterea interacţiunii cu alte instituţii academice externe şi stabilirea de noi colaborări legate de aria principală de cercetare a proiectului. • O3: Integrarea de nou conţinut în curriculumul didactic legat de domeniul ţintă al proiectului. Atragerea de studenţi din ciclurile avansate de studii în activităţi de cercetare. Domeniul tehnic ţintă: exemple de bază Fluxuri de date - evenimente (şi notificări asociate) : • creşterea sau scăderea unei cotaţii de bursă • schimbări în datele de monitorizare ale unui pacient • măsurarea unui nou kW pe un contor electric Domeniul tehnic ţintă: sisteme distribuite bazate pe evenimente Complex Event Processing (CEP) şi sisteme pub/sub: • Domenii de aplicaţie: software financiar, procesare de date în timp real, diseminarea şi execuţia tranzacţiilor în blockchain, etc. • Domenii conexe: optimizări în codificarea şi propagarea datelor, aspecte de confidenţialitate a datelor folosite, etc. • Aria principală generală: procesarea de fluxuri continue de evenimente cu focus pe trei direcţii primare: scalabilitate, toleranţă la căderi/erori şi aspecte de securitate. EBSIS – Plan de lucru EBSIS – Pachete de lucru principale şi activităţi esenţiale asociate WP1: Acţiuni primare de training • invitarea de colaboratori externi pentru activităţi de predare în regim bloc • iniţierea de co-supervizări cu parteneri externi pentru teze de disertaţie WP2: Acţiuni de specializare avansată • invitarea de experţi din cadrul partenerilor de proiect pentru susţinerea de seminarii ştiinţifice • vizite de lucru în grupuri de cercetare partenere • participarea în scop de specializare la conferinţe în zona domeniului ţintă a proiectului sau a celor conexe WP3: Activităţi cu impact extern • trei şcoli de vară • prezentări şi manifestări deschise în colaborare cu industria de profil • organizarea unei ediţii a unei conferinţe itinerante cunoscute în cursul ultimului an al proiectului EBSIS - Rezultate • Toate obiectivele proiectului au fost îndeplinite prin executarea activităţilor planificate, rezultatele şi impactul proiectului fiind apreciate de către comisia de evaluare • Impactul corelat al activităţilor proiectului cu activităţi colaborative şi de cercetare iniţiate în paralel: • Câştigarea de două ori (2017 şi 2018) a premiului DEBS Grand Challenge – principala competiţie academică internaţională anuală de profil pentru dezvoltarea de soluţii informatice în domeniul ţintă al proiectului • Atragerea studenţilor spre activităţi de cercetare în aria proiectului rezultate în lucrări ştiinţifice acceptate în proces peer-review în conferinţe internaţionale de top • Iniţierea de colaborări noi cu industria locală în activităţi corelate cu domeniul ţintă al proiectului • Iniţierea de noi colaborări în activităţi de cercetare cu membri ai partenerilor externi • Introducerea de noi cursuri conexe cu domeniul ţintă al proiectului în curriculum-ul instituţiei coordonatoare • ... şi altele EBSIS – Provocări (selectiv) Provocări generale administrative: • alinierea regulamentelor specifice programului de finanţare european Horizon 2020 cu legislaţia naţională, aspecte birocratice multiple în contextul varietăţii activităţilor organizate, etc. WP1 - Acţiuni primare de training: • integrarea activităţilor organizate în paralel cu programul didactic obişnuit (ca timp şi spaţiu de desfăşurare necesar) • captarea interesului studenţilor printr-o tematică nouă şi atractivă WP2 - Acţiuni de specializare avansată • sincronizarea în disponibilitatea ca timp a personalului implicat • extinderea ariilor de cercetare principale vizate spre cele conexe pentru atragerea unei categorii mai largi din grupurile de cercetare din cadrul instituţiilor participante WP3 - Activităţi cu impact extern • principiu cheie – planificare în avans (şi menţinerea de opţiuni rezervă): • Şcoli de vară – contactarea de experţi externi în vederea stabilirii programului de prezentări tehnice cu minim şase luni înaintea desfăşurării evenimentelor • Conferinţă itinerantă – contactarea de comitete permanente de conferinţă (steering committees) în vederea organizării cu doi ani înainte de organizarea evenimentului Mai multe informaţii disponibile în pagina proiectului: http://ebsis.info.uaic.ro/

documents.name: ECSEL Moore4Medical – Accelerate Innovation in Emerging Medical Devices with Open Technology Platforms
documents.textPreview: INCD pentru Microtehnologie- IMT Bucuresti - Proiect H2020 (www.imt.ro) Proiect H2020-ECSEL Moore4Medical - Accelerate Innovation in Emerging Medical Devices with Open Technology Platforms Proiect de tip ECSEL (ECSEL-2019-1-IA - ECSEL-2019-1-IA) Contract de finanțare: 876190 Valoare totala grant: € 66.084.693,20 Valoare partener IMT-București: € 1.300.000,00 Perioada de implementare: 2020 – 2023 Coordonatorul proiectului: Philips Electronics, Olanda https://moore4medical.eu/ Proiectul reunește 66 de parteneri (majoritatea fiind reprezentată de către companii) din Olanda, Italia, Irlanda, Spania, Belgia, Finlanda, Germania, Austria, Elveția, Portugalia, Ungaria și România. IMT-București este singurul partener român din cadrul consorțiului. Proiectul ECSEL Moore4Medical va accelera inovația în dispozitivele medicale electronice. Proiectul se adresează aplicațiilor și tehnologiilor emergente, care oferă noi oportunități pentru industria componentelor și sistemelor electronice cu aplicații biomedicale. Tehnologiile curente oferă o multitudine de oportunități pentru pacienți și pent ru industria medicală. Proiectul Moore4Medical încearcă să găsească modalitățile prin care acestea pot fi implementate eficient și viabil. Moore4Medical se va concentra pe dezvoltarea de platforme tehnologice deschise pentru aceste domenii emergente, care să permită depășirea limitărilor curente în timp mai scurt și la costuri cât mai mici. Ritmul inovării în ceea ce privește dezvoltarea dispozitivelor medicale este mult în urma celui din domeniul dispozitivelor electronice de uz larg. Din acest punct de v edere, relevanța principală a proiectului Moore4Medical este de a accelera inovarea în domeniul dispozitivelor medicale, prin dezvoltarea de platforme tehnologice deschise, pentru un număr atent selectat de domenii medicale emergente. În momentul de față granițele dintre industria farmaceutică, cea de tehnologii medicale și industria componentelor și sistemelor electronice se estompează. La intersecțiile dintre aceste domenii apar noi tehnologii care oferă oportunități mari pentru industrie, precum și pent ru societate, sub formă de asistență medicală mai bună și accesibilă, ceea ce face proiectul Moore4Medical extrem de relevant pentru necesitățile societății actuale. Principalele acțiuni din Moore4Medical: • Dispozitive implantabile - Medicamentele bioelectronice sunt mici dispozitive implantabile aplicate pe nervi care duc la diferite organe, cu scopul de a modula functia organului. Moore4Medical va aborda doua aspecte importante care lipsesc: dezvoltarea unei platforme tehnologice care sa furnizeze ef icient energie pentru implanturi si stimularea selectiva a nervilor periferici; • Organe-pe-chip - În dispozitivele OOC (organ -on-chip), functia de baza a unui organ este reprodusa în cea mai simpla forma dintr-un cip cuprinzând microfluidice, senzori si celule. În Moore4Medical va fi dezvoltata o platforma care sa asigure infrastructura electronica si fluidica pentru astfel de dispozitive: • „Drug adherence” – asigurarea respectării planului de tratament - Nerespectarea medicamentatiei prescrise este o problem a grava care afecteaza nu numai pacientul, ci si sistemul de asistenta medicala. În Moore4Medical va fi dezvoltata o platforma care sa monitorizeze si sa îmbunatateasca aderenta medicamentelor; • O nouă generație de dispozitive medicale cu ultrasunete - Dezvoltarea ecografiei MEMS (CMUT / PMUT) cu productie pe scara larga la preturi accesibile traductoarele provoaca o schimbare de paradigma în imagistica cu ultrasunete. În Moore4Medical va fi dezvoltat un sistem reconfigurabil de imagistica cu ultrasunete, care utilizeaza ecografia 3D si inteligenta artificiala pentru a ajuta la achizitia si interpretarea imaginilor cu ultrasunete; • Chirurgia fără raze X - La aproape 125 de ani dupa ce Wilhelm Röntgen a realizat prima imagine cu raze X, imagistica cu raze X ionizante ramâne în continuare modalitatea imagistica primara. În Moore4Medical vor fi dezvoltate doua platforme care folosesc lumina în loc de raze X pentru a ghida interventiile chirurgicale. Primul sistem se bazeaza pe detectarea formei optice (OSS). Cel de-al doilea sistem urmareste optic instrumentele cu ajutorul unor camere foto, eliminând considerabil nevoia de imagistica cu raze X; • Monitorizarea continuă a pacienților - Una dintre premisele esentiale pentru a reduce spitalizarea este monitorizarea cont inua si discreta a semnelor vitale ale unei persoane. Monitorizarea persoanelor în timpul somnului poate produce o sursa bogata de informatii. În Moore4Medical va fi dezvoltata o platforma de teledetectie care utilizeaza o multitudine de senzori pentru a colecta eficient si discret datele despre pacienti. Implicarea INCD pentru Microtehnologie in cadrul proiectului Moore4Medical: IMT are deja o poziție importantă în domeniul cercetării și dezvoltării europene în micro - și nanosisteme. Pe termen mediu, ca urmare a implementării proiectului Moore4Medical, preconizăm valorificarea rezultatelor obținute prin extinderea portofoliului nostru de servicii tehnologice în domeniul electrozilor implantabili și aplicațiilor de tip organ-pe-chip. Grupul din cadrul IMT -Bucuresti care lucreaza in proiectul Moore4Medical ( Laboratorul de Microsisteme pentru Aplicatii Biomedicale si de Mediu ) este implicat in doua dintre directiile principale ale proiectului, si anume Dispozitive Implantabile si Organe pe Chip. IMT va folosi rezultatele proiectului pentru a valida expertiza sa în domeniul micro - și nanosistemelor pentru aplicații biomedicale, în principal prin: • Tehnologie îmbunătățită pentru electrozi implantabli și electronică de detecție; • Tehnologie îmbunătățită pentru acoperiri biocompatibile; • Noi cunoștințe și modele / studii de caz de simulare pentru aplicații de tip organ-pe-chip; • Noi rezultate tehnico-științifice, cu diseminare în jurnale și la conferințe. Rezultate intermediare: In cadrul activitatilor de dezvoltare a dispozitivelor implantabile, IMT a contribuit la definirea unui proiect initial al unor noi tipuri de electrozi implantabili cu aplicatii neurologice. Electrozii au fost configurati, au fost stabilite tehnici de asamblare si incapsulare prin metoda soft encapsulation (acoperire cu m ateriale flexibile). Materialele utilizate la incapsulare sunt atat flexibile, cat si biocompatibile (de ex. Poliamida). Pe partea de dispozitive de tip organe-pe-chip, IMT a contribuit la definirea specificatiilor initiale ale unor componente ale sistemelor microfluidice care vor reprezenta organele artificiale dezvoltate pe un chip. In perioada imediat urmatoare, vom derula in principal activitati de modelare – simulare, care vor testa in mod virtual functionalitatea componentelor propuse si vor contribui la optimizarea acestora.

documents.name: eDREAM – enabling new Demand REsponse Advanced, Market oriented and secure technologies, solutions and business models
documents.textPreview: The eDREAM project is co-funded by the EU’s Horizon 2020 innovation programme under grant agreement No. 774478. Tehnologii inovative de Demand Response pentru un ecosistem energetic descentralizat eDREAM – enabling new Demand REsponse Advanced, Market oriented and secure technologies, solutions and business models 2Copyright eDREAM consortium Despre proiect ■ Titlul proiectului: eDREAM – enabling new Demand REsponse Advanced, Market oriented and secure technologies, solutions and business models ■ Program: Horizon 2020 Research & Innovation ■ Durata: 36 luni ■ Valoarea proiectului: 3,822,125 € ■ Coordonator: Engineering – Ingegneria Informatica SPA, Italia ■ Parteneri: 10 – Italia (Engineering – Ingegneria Informatica SPA, Italia, Energy@Work, ASM Terni, Emotion), Spania (ATOS), Grecia (The Centre for Research and Technology-Hellas - CERTH), UK (Teesside University, KIWI Power), Romania (Servelect ESCO, Universitatea Tehnică din Cluj-Napoca) 3Copyright eDREAM consortium Despre proiect 4Copyright eDREAM consortium Scopul proiectului Proiectul eDREAM își propune să dezvolte noi soluții pentru Operatorii de distribuție a energiei, și să îmbunătățească procesul de luare a deciziilor pentru Agregatorii și Furnizorii de energie, utilizând un nou ecosistem energetic descentralizat, prin integrarea completă a micro-gridurilor și a VPP-urilor (centrale electrice virtuale) în rețeaua de energie locală. Principalele active ale proiectului sunt: • Piețe de energie locale flexibile create în special pentru Operatorii de Distribuție și Agregatori. • Piețe de energie locale peer to peer adaptate pentru Prosumatori și Agregatori. • Optimizarea centralelor electrice virtuale (VPP) prin coaliții dinamice, adaptate Agregatorilor. documents.textPreview: ROMÂNIA een.ec.europa.eu PROIECTE DERULATE SUB EGIDA ENTERPRISE EUROPE NETWORK Agenția pentru Dezvoltare Regională Sud -Vest Oltenia este partener al Rețelei Enterprise Europe Network din ianuarie 2015 și alături de Agenț ia pentru Dezvoltare Regională Vest (în calitate de lider ), Centrul Regional de Inovare și Transfer Tehnologic – Tehimpuls, Camera de Comerț, Industrie și Agricultură Arad și Universitatea din Craiova formează Cosorțiul Ro-Boost SMEs prin intermediul căruia implementează proiectele comune “Ro-Boost SMEs - Boosting Smart and Innovation -Driven Gr owth for Romanian SMEs”, finanțat prin Programul COSME și „Ro-Boost Inno SMEs – Boosting the Innovative Potential of Romanian SMEs” , finanțat prin Programul Orizont 2020. Enterprise Europe Network (EEN) este o inițiativă a Comisiei Europene și reprezintă cea mai mare rețea care sprijină întreprinderile din peste 60 de țări din întreaga lume, punându -le la dispoziție un set de servicii gratuite de promovare, informare, sprijin și consiliere în vederea accesării de noi piețe și parteneri. Agenția pentru Dezvoltare Regională Sud -Vest Oltenia, prin derularea proiectului ”Ro- Boost SMEs - Boosting Smart and Innovation-Driven Growth for Romanian SMEs”, sub egida Enterprise Europe Network , urmărește sprijinirea IMM -urilor de la nive lul Regiunii Sud-Vest Oltenia, în vederea internaționalizării afacerilor și creșterii competitivității în termeni de capacitate inovativă, dinamică partenerială și valorificare a finanțărilor disponibile, punând la dispoziția acestora, următoarele servicii gratuite: Enterprise Europe Network een.ec.europa.eu  Servicii de consiliere, activități de sprijin și informare Prin intermediul activității de helpdesk, de la nivelul ADR Sud -Vest Oltenia, reprezentanții IMM-urilor regionale beneficiază de sprijin, suport și informare cu privire la diverse tem e europene de interes pentru aceștia, precum: legislația și politicile europene, oportunitățile de finanțare europene, accesarea piețelor internaționale, accesul la finanțare, îmbunătățirea capacității de management.  Servicii de facilitare a parteneriatel or transnaționale pentru afaceri, transfer tehnologic și inovare Experții din cadrul echipei de implementare a proiectului Ro-Boost SMEs sprijină IMM -urile în identificarea de parteneri în alte state UE sau asociate, cu ajutorul unor instrumente de interm ediere specifice Rețelei Enterprise Europe Network: formulare de parteneriat, expresii de interes, instrument online pentru identificarea oportunităților de afaceri. Rețeaua Enterprise Europe Network pune la dispoziția reprezentanților companiilor cinci formulare de parteneriat pe care aceștia sunt invitați să le completeze, cu sprijinul experților EEN, în funcție de interesele lor de colaborare, în vederea publicării pe platforma rețelei și identificării de noi parteneri de afaceri. De asemenea, reprezenta nții companiilor au posibilitatea de a completa, personal sau cu ajutorul experților EEN, expresii de interes pentru cele peste 10.000 de profiluri (cereri și oferte de produse/tehnologii și servicii) ale companiilor din aria de acoperire a Rețelei Enterpr ise Europe Network, deja publicate pe platformă. Motorul de căutare ”Find a partner abroad for your business”, disponibil în cadrul platformei, oferă companiilor posibilitatea de a identifica, în mod individual, noi parteneri pentru dezvoltarea propriei ac tivități. Instrumentul oferă acces nelimitat la bazele de date ale Comisiei Europene referitoare la cereri și oferte de cooperare în afaceri, transfer tehnologic și propuneri de proiecte în domeniul cercetării, inovării și dezvoltării. Enterprise Europe Network een.ec.europa.eu Avantajul utilizării acestei platforme de internaționalizare a parteneriatelor de afaceri este acela că elaborarea și înscrierea unui profil, precum și gestionarea expresiilor de interes sunt activități facilitate în totalitate de membrii Enterprise Europe Network, asigurând confidențialitatea și relevanța contactelor stabilite. Totodată, în vederea facilitării parteneriatelor transnaționale pentru IMM -urile regionale, ADR Sud -Vest Oltenia urmărește organizarea de evenimente de brokeraj și misiuni economice. IMM -urile participante sunt sprijinite în: pregătirea unui profil de cooperare atractiv și înregistrarea la eveniment; identificarea participanților de interes; pre -stabilirea de întâlniri bilaterale; asistență pe întreaga durată a evenimentului, inclusiv în negocierea parteneriatelor, dacă este cazul. Compa niile interesate pot participa și la alte evenimente de brokeraj sau misiuni economice organizate periodic la nivelul rețelei pe diverse domenii de activitate.  Activități de feedback din partea IMM-urilor Experții EEN de la nivelul ADR Sud -Vest Oltenia diseminează către IMM -uri chestionarele inițiate de către Comisia Europeană, cu scopul de a crește gradul de participare a IMM-urilor la demersurile Uniunii Eur opene de consultare a mediului economic pe teme de interes pentr u acestea. Opiniile reprezentanț ilor mediului de afacer i de la nivel regional privind îmbunătățirea legislaț iei europene pentru mediul de afaceri sunt colectate periodic, prin consultări publice și transmise către factorii decizionali europeni.  Servicii privind creșterea inovării în cadrul IMM-urilor Acesta este un se rviciu separat , finanțat prin Programul Orizont 2020, dedicat cercetării și inovării. Obiectivul acestui tip de serviciu îl reprezintă creșterea capacităț ii de inovare a IMM-urilor, precum și a capacității de management al inovării. Enterprise Europe Network een.ec.europa.eu În acest sens, Agenția pentru Dezvoltare Regională Sud -Vest Oltenia implementează, conform unui acord -cadru încheiat între Comisia Europeană și pa rtenerii Consorțiului Ro - Boost SMEs , proiectul „Ro-Boost Inno SMEs – Boosting the Innovative Potential of Romanian SMEs” , prin care pune la dispoziția IMM -urilor regionale servicii gratuite, dedicate, de îmbunătățire a capacității de management al inovării. Cele două tipuri de pachete de sprijin pentru IMM -uri din cadrul proiectului Ro -Boost Inno SMEs au fost dezvoltate cu scopul de a ajuta companiile să crească și să accelereze rentabilitățile economice din inovare, prin îmbunătățirea capacităților lor de management al inovării, utilizând metodologii dovedite, de înaltă calitate. Cele două tipuri de pachete de sprijin sunt:  Asistență pentru companii în vederea îmbunătățirii capacității de a gestiona inovarea (EIMC) , prin furnizare de servicii specializate d e evaluare a managementului inovării (utilizând instrumentul IMP³ROVE) și realizarea de recomandări care vizează îmbunătățirea performanțelor economice.  Asistență pentru companii beneficiare ale finanțărilor prin intermediul Instrumentului pentru IMM -uri (KAM), prin furnizare de servicii de mentorat (coaching) care să le permită atingerea unui anumit nivel de pregătire în vederea obținerii gradului de inovare așteptat. Companiile beneficiază de servicii specializate de evaluare a nevoilor de asistență teh nică, de identificarea și recomandarea unor „coach” potriviți (specialiști recunoscuți în Uniunea Europeană), care le pot acorda consultanță în vederea implementării cu succes a proiectului inovator dezvoltat în etapele anterioare. În ceea ce privește asi stența pentru companii în vederea îmbunătățirii capacității de a gestiona inovarea, experții de la nivelul ADR Sud -Vest Oltenia utilizează instrumentele Academiei IMP³ROVE, care oferă cea mai complexă metodă de evaluare și creștere a performanței managementului inovării existentă la nivel european și recunoscută de Comisia Europeană. Enterprise Europe Network een.ec.europa.eu După ce a beneficiat de servicii privind creșterea inovării, compania va putea să își gestioneze procesele de inovare internă, astfel încât acestea să devină parte integrantă a strategiei de dezvoltare și creștere a afacerii. Scopul este de a face companiile inovatoare mai competitive și de a le ajuta să crească. Pentru informații suplimentare referitoare la serviciile și oportunitățile of erite prin proiectele Ro-Boost SMEs și Ro-Boost Inno SMEs vă invităm să vizitați website -ul consorțiului - www.eenroboost.ro.

documents.textPreview: Grant Agreement number: 676555 Project acronym: EMSODEV Project title: EMSO implementation and operation: DEVelopment of instrument module Call: H2020-INFRADEV-1-2015-1 under H2020-EU.1.4.1.1.- Developing new world -class research infrastructures Programme Topic: INFRADEV-3-2015 - Individual implementation and operation of ESFRI projects Start date of the project: 1 September 2015 Duration of the project: 48 months End date: 31 August 2019 Coordinator: INSTITUTO NAZIONALE DI GEOFISICA E VULCANOLOGIA, Italy Consortium: 11 partners from 9 countries (link: http://www.emsodev.eu/partnership.html ) Total Budget: 4,529,864.98 Euro Project website address: http://www.emsodev.eu/ EU website about the project: https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/676555 Communication materials: - Project’s brochure: http://www.emsodev.eu/Files/Brochure/EMSODEV-Brochure.pdf - Flyer about EGIM: http://www.emsodev.eu/Files/Brochure/EGIM%20Brochure.pdf - Newsletters: http://www.emsodev.eu/newsletters.html - Project video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A2nEBkCwq2M - EGIM video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jfrfl81wndo (YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCsLV-a6AFSGJHxoUpxUYtMg) Summary of the context and overall objectives of the project EMSO ERIC provides power, communications, sensors and data infrastructure for continuous, high - resolution, (near)real -time, interactive ocean observations across a multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary range of research areas including biology, geology, chemistry, physics, engineering and computer science, from polar to subtropical environments, through the water column to th e abyss. Coordination among the 11 EMSO ERIC Regional Facilities (RFs) (8 deep sea and 3 shallow test sites) has been strengthened through the EMSODEV project, which has designed and produced three EMSO Generic Instrument Modules (EGIMs). The EMSODEV general objective was to catalyse the full implementation and operation of the EMSO ERIC distributed Research Infrastructure (RI) through the development, testing and deployment of EGIMs. These modules provide accurate, consistent, comparable and long -term meas urements of Essential Ocean Variables (EOVs), which are key to addressing urgent societal and scientific challenges, such as climate change, ocean ecosystem disturbance, and marine hazards. This results in the increased interoperability of EMSO ERIC nodes due to the harmonized collection of EOV time series. The specific objectives of EMSODEV were to: (1) Design and implement a state-of-the-art, standardized multidisciplinary EGIM (2) Fully test, calibrate, validate and assess the effectiveness of this innovative module (3) Use the Big Ocean Data produced by the harmonized instrument module as a catalyst to strengthen the data management and delivery backbone of the EMSO RI (4) Promote the uptake of the project results and public -private partnerships, establishing links with industry and SMEs for technology transfer and future RDI activities. Work performed from the beginning to the end of the project and main results achieved - EMSODEV realized an EGIM prototype followed by two replicas. The EGIMs constitute a significant step beyond standardised and interoperable monitoring systems at the EMSO ERIC RFs. - A Data Management Platform (DMP) and related tools (SMD -Sensor Monitor Dashboard and MOODA-Module for Ocean Observatory Data Analysis) were fully implemented. - A Joint Ownership Management Agreement (JOMA) was agreed and is currently being signed by the relevant EMSODEV partners. This is a first step in passing the ownership and the legacy of EMSODEV to the EMSO ERIC. - EGIM technical specifications defined and a prototype built accordingly. - Lab tested and shallow-water was successfully tested at OBSEA for 6 months. Then two replicated EGIMs were realized through an open tender, won by a SME. - An EGIM 2-day School was organised for scientists and technicians to provide effective training on the EGIM deployment, configuration and management. - Three EMSO sites were selected for the EGIM deployments: Azores, PLOCAN and Western Ionian, with the aim to test them in different configurations (seafloor stand -alone, moored and seafloor cabled). The EMSO Azores one -year experiment was concluded from 2017 to August 2018 . All collected data are accessible via the EMSO France data portal, are visualised and explored using MOODA. In PLOCAN two-phase deployment was undertaken. In Phase1 one EGIM was deployed in an harbour in shallow water for 47 days. The acquired data were displayed in real time. In Phase2 EGIM was deployed in 45m. The final deployment at 3650m at the ESTOC site will take place before the end of 2019 (depending on the ship availability and the appropriate sea state conditions). - In Western Ionian all the preparatory activities were successfully concluded and the deployment is awaiting suitable sea conditions and logistics. One of the main issues for installation at greater depth is the availability of a suitable vessel equipped with ROV able to perform instal lation and cable connections. Work has been carried out to prepare the EGIM installation to a deep infrastructure equipped with optical communication system for data transmission in real time. The partner in charge is strongly committed to this final deployment relevant for EMSO ERIC, being the only experiment in cabled mode at >2000m. - The EMSODEV DMP was defined, modelled and implemented throughout the project. DMP ingests, consolidates, processes and archives data coming from the EGIMs, integrates the EMS O RFs data management architectures and makes data available to the EMSO portal and to other initiatives (e.g. EMODNET). - Two tools were implemented, SMD and MOODA. SMD assists technicians to check if EGIM is working correctly. MOODA helps scientists download and analyse data. - The EMSO Metadata Catalogue is maintained , all EMSODEV data are archived and accessed at PANGAEA https://www.pangaea.de/?q=emsodev and EMSO adheres to Big Ocean Data FAIR principles - The communication and dissemination focused on the dissemination of the project activities and its results to the scientific community, industry and to the general public. Also the EMSODEV results were very broadly communicated through various channels at many events. - Initially a detailed business case study report was compiled, assessing market applications and commercialization opportunities for the EGIM in areas like ocean energy, seabed mining and marine monitoring for environmental protection/study. S everal technology transfer activities have been undertaken increasing the contact between EMSO partners and end-users. - Exploitation Plan (EP) was produced and relates to the delivery and commercialisation of EGIM infrastructure to research organisations and private sector. The EP includes a detailed report IPR and JOMA. Photo: EGIM frame and NEMO-SN1 Infrastructure at Western Ionian site Photo: EMSO EGIM deployed in shallow water Progress beyond the state of the art and expected potential impact (including the socio -economic impact and the wider societal implications of the project so far)  EMSODEV was a fundamental contribution to advance the construction of EMSO ERIC through an EGIM new observational component and a unified DMP. The EMSODEV results confirm this impact as the activities are a first step in the development of services offered by the EMS O ERIC.  EMSODEV has produced high -quality, standardized and fully traceable and easy -accessible data and will produce reliable data products for modelling and model calibrations in the future. This will allow EMSO ERIC to be a competitive player in the gl obal science and the stakeholder communities.  The DMP and tools (SMD and MOODA) facilitate researchers to obtain time -series data streams and user-oriented tools to speed -up data preparation before the scientists' original processing.  The EMSODEV consortium is transferring its results to the EMSO ERIC, an important step in this process is the JOMA.  EMSODEV activities have been implemented in collaboration with SMEs: the COSTOF2, the core of EGIM, was built by a French SME and two EGIMs were replicated by an Italian SME. The SMEs gained valuable experience in development of equipment for long -term deployment at sea, enhancing European capability to develop fixed-point infrastructure. This may have been a key step in providing joint-collaboration with SMEs for joint R&D initiatives in the future.  EMSO ERIC signed a MoU with Ocean Networks Canada (ONC). ONC has shown a strong interest to use the EGIM platform in key locations in Arctic.  EMSODEV has provide training opportunities for scientists and technicians, building capacity within the EMSO ERIC community and facilitating proactive development of the mobility of researchers for the ultimate goal of building excellence and underpinning capacity building. Several key dates: Photo: EMSODEV Kick off meeting 22-23 September 2015 in Heraklion, Crete - On September 22, 2015 at Heraklion, Greece the representatives of the nine European countries, members of the research infrastructure consortium EMSO (European Multidisciplinary Sea floor and watercolumn Observatory) met in Crete to launch a European Union 2020 Horizon initialy three, then four year project, EMSODEV which intended to enable the full implementation and operation of EMSO. EMSO members had launched this project which aim ed to become of the largest and most reliable programs of sea water monitoring in the world. - On January 21 , 2016, the European Research Infrastructure Consortium (ERIC) Committee approved the EMSO’s request to become an ERIC, thus closing step 2 of the multi-year application process. It is now in the hands of the European Commission to give the final approval and publish the Statutes in the Official Journal of the European Union. France, Greece, UK, Ireland, and Italy are now full members of the ERIC, wh ereas Portugal, Romania and Spain are completing the application process. - On March 10, 2016 EMSO was recognized by The European Strategy Forum for Research Infrastructures (ESFRI) as an ESFRI Landmark. The announcement was made during the launch of the 2016 ESFRI Roadmap hosted by the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW) at its headquarters in Amsterdam. "It is a great honour and reward for the constant eff ort of the EMSO participating countries to receive such an important recognition'' said Paolo Favali, current coordinator of the programme EMSO and EMSODEV project. "The upcoming launch of EMSO ERIC will soon seal this huge collaborative engagement" . Paolo Favali added "The Research Infrastructures environmental landscape is the fundamen tal prerequisite for running marine science at top level in Europe." (ESFRI identifies research facilities of pan -European importance that are necessary to strengthen scientific excellence and competitiveness in the EU. - - A major step forward in the direct ocean observing has been taken with the deployment and installation of the new observatory infrastructure- EMSO Generic Instrument Module (EGIM), thus contributing to a standardised approach for European ocean observatories On the 1 st of December 2016 a major step forward in the direct ocean observing was taken with the deployment of the new observatory infrastructure, an ocean monitoring multi -sensor module EMSO Generic Instrument Module (EGIM) and its installation and maintenance on the OBSEA underwater observatory near the coast of Villanova i la Geltrú (Barcelona, Spain). After EGIM have undergone various and rigorous dry tests in laboratories, it will be tested on the observatory’s real- life conditions and each result will be checked and analysed, ensuring that EGIM will be able to function as required. The innovative open new opportunities for research and industry. The EGIM data will be accessible to all through an online Data Management Platform. Also, the standardised nature, timely processing and data delivery capability of the monitoring. - The EGIM prototype was deployed on the EMSO Azores observatory during this year maintenance cruise, on the 17 th of July 2017. The EGIM prototype was deployed in autonomous mode 15m South West from the hydrothermal vent site Seamon East node, 25m South West of the active edifice Tour Eiffel site on the Lucky Strike vent field. The objective of the EGIM deployment here was to monitor local hydrodynamic variability. The EGIM deployed on EMSO Azores observatory was the prototype built and tested by Ifremer and deployed on OBSEA cabled observatory during 6 months (October 2016 – March 2017). - After the EGIM prototype was deployment on the EMSO Azores observatory during the July 2017 maintenance cruise, its recovery was carried out according to a precise schedule in August 2018. Mechanical aspects were observed, complete sets of data were analyzed , regarding the oxygen optode, precise pressure sensor, hydrophone, COSTOF2, technical data, conductivity, temperature and pressure probe, turbidity sensor, ADCP. Also additional test concerning RDI workhorse ADCP were performed. - On the 16th of June 2019, the EGIM was deployed on the PLOCAN Test Site East of Gran Canarias (Canary Islands). EGIM is able to operate on any EMSO node, mooring line, sea bed station, cabled or standalone and/or with a surface buoy. It is the first time the EGIM has been deployed in stand- alone mode. The system was be recovered mid -August and mid-September 2019, expecting the best weather conditions within that time-window, and the data will then be downloaded from the system for analysis. GeoEcoMar was a partner in EMSODEV project, having a total budget of 180,226.25 Euro. GeoEcoMar was involved in WP2 - Requirement definition and specification , Task 2.1 System Requirements of the EMSO nodes , Task 2.2 Scientific Parameters Requirements, Task 2.4 Technical specification of the generic instrument module, WP3 - EMSO Generic instrument Module, Task 3.4 Dry and wet testing of EGIM prototype , WP4 - EGIM shallow water performance assessment and validation, Task 4.1 Primary Test plan and operational procedures handbook, Task 4.3 EMSO Generic instrument module (EGIM) shallow water testing and evaluation , WP5 - EGIM Replication and in situ performance evaluation, Task 5.1 Selection of EMSO nodes, WP6 - Data Management platform and related services , Task 6.1 Data management plan , Task 6.5 Interoperability with existing EMSO local data nodes, WP8 - Exploitation and Commercialisation, Task 8.2 Users profiling, Task 8.3 Networking. The major involvement was as WP leader in WP7, Task 7.1: Implementation of the Dissemination plan, Task 7.2 Communication activities. The activities from this work package aimed to an “effective communication and dissemination of the steps to be taken by the new pan -European Research Infrastructure EMSO -ERIC” increasing the visibility towards the scientific community, the policy makers and business communities, as well as to the wider public. Photo: A page from the brochure Photo: The cover page of the EGIM flyer EMSODEV project was present at AGU (American Geophysical Union), the largest Earth and space science meeting in the world that took place on 11 -15 December 2017 in New Orleans, Louisiana. GeoEcoMar, as part of EMSODEV project attended this important conference, taking the opportunity to present the importance of EMSODEV project at European and regional level. Putting Romania and the Black Sea on the AGU map opens new opportunities to show the research of natural marine hazards in this area, together with their high importance at European level by being part of the EMSODEV project. The Paper title: “A nalysis of Complex Marine Hazards on the Romanian Black Sea Shelf Using Combined Geophysical Methods”. The abstract link: https://agu.confex.com/agu/fm17/meetingapp.cgi/Paper/231255 - The conference "Sustainable Development at the Black Sea" - SUST-BLACK, organized by GeoEcoMar under the auspices of the Romanian Presidency of the Council of Europe, took place in Bucharest on May 8-11, 2019. The event was supported by the European Commission and the Ministry of Research and Innovation, being hosted at the Palace of Parliament. On of May 8 was presented the section "European Coastal and Marine Research Infrastructures – major support for excellence in Marine Research in the Black Se a." – including presentation and panel discussion with speakers representing different research infrastructures and networks, including Juan José Dañobeitia, EMSO ERIC Director -General. On May 9 a special presentation was dedicated to the EMSO ERIC research infrastructure, were EMSODEV results were also mentioned, speaker being again, Mr. Dañobeitia. Both presentations were live streamed online by different channels. - A special event was, as stipulated in the Grant Agreement, a final one -day conference organized in Romania, in Constanta, near the Black Sea, where the EMSO ERIC facility is. The conference was organized by GeoEcoMar and the hosts were Vlad Rădulescu, the coordinator of the project for GeoEcoMar and Mirela Dinicoiu, responsible of the commun ication and dissemination aspects of the project. On August 26, 2019 a national conference took place on the occasion of the finalisation of the EMSODEV project. National stakeholders were invited, representing academic, institutional and business communit ies. During the conference the main results obtained in the EMSODEV project have been presented - with an emphasis on EGIM, but there the results for each work package were detailed. The event represented the occasion to present of the main results obtained in the EMSODEV project, to provide technical details and practical utility of the obtained results - emphasis on EGIM. The conference was ended with the conclusions and free discussions on the implementation of the results of the EMSODEV project. The latest success story published by the EU website was the EMSODEV one: "Sensing module keeps watch beneath the waves". The European Union's website regularly presents articles on successful European research and innovation projects that have received European funding. One of them was the H2020 project EMSODEV. https://ec.europa.eu/research/infocentre/article_en.cfm?artid=53925 More results, including the communication and dissemination activities, a joint effort of all the partners from the consortium are to be found here, on the European Union webpage: https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/676555/results
